gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
gaps.explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.

gaps.sentence: The stolen car ___ (find) abandoned in a car park this morning.
gaps.explanation: 'This morning' (now over) takes past simple passive: was + found.

gaps.sentence: All the passwords ___ (reset) after last week's security breach.
gaps.hint: recent past, plural subject, present relevance
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have been + reset for a recently completed action.

gaps.sentence: The results ___ (publish) on the university website next Friday.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'Next Friday' fixes the future reference.

gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.
The results receive the action: 'will be announced'.
